\chapter{Looking and reading}
\label{ch:zh-looking-reading}
\hlchaptermodality{18}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can understand, say, read and write \zh{看}, \zh{看见}, \zh{好看}, \zh{书} and \zh{看书}, and score listening, speaking, reading and writing separately.}

Two carefully staged characters support five nearby meanings, expanding retrieval and separate listening, speaking, cold-reading and no-model writing scores.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[kàn]{Hear \emph{kàn} — look or watch}

\label{lesson:ZH-C18-hear-kan}



\begin{quote}
Say \textbf{Chinese language} and \textbf{China} in Mandarin. Keep those answers separate, then put the cards away.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\emph{kàn} — \textbf{look at; watch}
\end{quote}

Start high and let the tone fall cleanly. The written form stays hidden in this first step so sound and meaning can settle before handwriting begins.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://hsk.cn-bj.ufileos.com/3.0/\%E6\%96\%B0\%E7\%89\%88HSK\%E8\%80\%83\%E8\%AF\%95\%E5\%A4\%A7\%E7\%BA\%B21219.pdf}{Official HSK 3.0 syllabus, Level 1 vocabulary}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[kàn]{\zh{看} — a hand above an eye}

\label{lesson:ZH-W18-kan-observe}



\begin{quote}
Say \textbf{look or watch} as \emph{kàn}. Then write the familiar \textbf{\zh{中}} once and put it away before meeting the new shape.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script — the shape}
Write \textbf{\zh{看}} in nine strokes. Make the short top stroke first, then the two crossing strokes and the long left fall above. Finish with \textbf{\zh{目}} below: left, top-and-right, two inner bars, bottom. Nine strokes; eight lifts.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Trace \textbf{\zh{看}} once. Say \textbf{hand above, eye below} while keeping the lower box wide enough for its two inner bars.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chanind/hanzi-writer-data/68d10a4b21150cae5e1ebbd223eed289cf32d90c/data/\%E7\%9C\%8B.json}{Hanzi Writer Data \zh{看}, pinned stroke paths and medians}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[kàn]{\zh{看} — copy hand above, eye below}

\label{lesson:ZH-W18-kan-guided}



\begin{quote}
Read \textbf{\zh{中文}} and give its meaning. Then air-write \textbf{hand above, eye below}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Copy \textbf{\zh{看}} twice beside the model. On the second copy, pause before \textbf{\zh{目}} and check that the long falling stroke points toward the eye rather than through it.

\subsection*{Your turn — Spaced Return}
Hear \textbf{Chinese language with \zh{中}} and write \zh{中文} once without pinyin.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chanind/hanzi-writer-data/68d10a4b21150cae5e1ebbd223eed289cf32d90c/data/\%E7\%9C\%8B.json}{Hanzi Writer Data \zh{看}, pinned stroke paths and medians}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[kàn]{\zh{看} — wait, then recover the eye}

\label{lesson:ZH-W18-kan-delayed}



\begin{quote}
Write \textbf{\zh{中国}} from the meaning \textbf{China}. Then look at \textbf{\zh{看}} for five seconds and cover it.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say \textbf{hand above, eye below}, then write \textbf{\zh{看}} once without the model. Reveal it only after all nine strokes. Repair only the first mismatch.

\subsection*{Your turn — Spaced Return}
Hear \textbf{China} once more and write \zh{中国} without a model.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chanind/hanzi-writer-data/68d10a4b21150cae5e1ebbd223eed289cf32d90c/data/\%E7\%9C\%8B.json}{Hanzi Writer Data \zh{看}, pinned stroke paths and medians}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[kàn]{\zh{看} — the familiar sound meets the shape}

\label{lesson:ZH-C18-kan}



\begin{quote}
Say \textbf{look at or watch} in Mandarin.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\zh{看}} — \emph{kàn} — \textbf{look at; watch}
\end{quote}

Hide the pinyin. Read \zh{看} from the hand-over-eye shape, say the falling tone, then give the meaning. One form now connects listening, speaking, reading, and writing.
\end{cousinweb}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Hear \emph{kàn}. Wait three seconds, then write \textbf{\zh{看}} once without a model.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://hsk.cn-bj.ufileos.com/3.0/\%E6\%96\%B0\%E7\%89\%88HSK\%E8\%80\%83\%E8\%AF\%95\%E5\%A4\%A7\%E7\%BA\%B21219.pdf}{Official HSK 3.0 syllabus, Level 1 vocabulary}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[kànjiàn]{Hear \emph{kànjiàn} — see}

\label{lesson:ZH-C18-hear-kanjian}



\begin{quote}
Say \textbf{look or watch} as \emph{kàn}, then say \textbf{goodbye} as \emph{zàijiàn}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\emph{kànjiàn} — \textbf{see; catch sight of}
\end{quote}

Both syllables fall. The familiar \emph{jiàn} now follows \emph{kàn}: you look and successfully perceive. Keep the characters hidden for this sound-first step.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://hsk.cn-bj.ufileos.com/3.0/\%E6\%96\%B0\%E7\%89\%88HSK\%E8\%80\%83\%E8\%AF\%95\%E5\%A4\%A7\%E7\%BA\%B21219.pdf}{Official HSK 3.0 syllabus, Level 1 vocabulary}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[kànjiàn]{\zh{看见} — looking reaches seeing}

\label{lesson:ZH-C18-kanjian}



\begin{quote}
Say \textbf{see} as \emph{kànjiàn}. Write \zh{看}, then point to \zh{见} in \zh{再见}.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\zh{看见}} — \emph{kànjiàn} — \textbf{see; catch sight of}
\end{quote}

Read the two known shapes from left to right. \zh{看} supplies looking; \zh{见} marks the perceived result.
\end{cousinweb}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Copy \textbf{\zh{看见}} once. Leave a clear boundary between the nine-stroke \zh{看} and the four-stroke \zh{见}.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://hsk.cn-bj.ufileos.com/3.0/\%E6\%96\%B0\%E7\%89\%88HSK\%E8\%80\%83\%E8\%AF\%95\%E5\%A4\%A7\%E7\%BA\%B21219.pdf}{Official HSK 3.0 syllabus, Level 1 vocabulary}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[hǎokàn]{Hear \emph{hǎokàn} — good-looking}

\label{lesson:ZH-C18-hear-haokan}



\begin{quote}
Say \textbf{good}, \textbf{look}, and \textbf{see} as three separate Mandarin answers.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\emph{hǎokàn} — \textbf{good-looking; nice to look at}
\end{quote}

Let \emph{hǎo} dip, then let \emph{kàn} fall. This is a description, not an instruction to look. The characters wait until the next tiny step.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://hsk.cn-bj.ufileos.com/3.0/\%E6\%96\%B0\%E7\%89\%88HSK\%E8\%80\%83\%E8\%AF\%95\%E5\%A4\%A7\%E7\%BA\%B21219.pdf}{Official HSK 3.0 syllabus, Level 1 vocabulary}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[hǎokàn]{\zh{好看} — good to look at}

\label{lesson:ZH-C18-haokan}



\begin{quote}
Say \textbf{good-looking} as \emph{hǎokàn}. Write \zh{好} and \zh{看} separately.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\zh{好看}} — \emph{hǎokàn} — \textbf{good-looking; nice to look at}
\end{quote}

No new character is hiding here. Read \zh{好}, then \zh{看}, and let the literal pieces carry you to the whole meaning.
\end{cousinweb}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Copy \textbf{\zh{好看}} once. Keep both characters full-sized instead of squeezing \zh{看}.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://hsk.cn-bj.ufileos.com/3.0/\%E6\%96\%B0\%E7\%89\%88HSK\%E8\%80\%83\%E8\%AF\%95\%E5\%A4\%A7\%E7\%BA\%B21219.pdf}{Official HSK 3.0 syllabus, Level 1 vocabulary}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[Practice]{Retrieval 1 — look, see, or good-looking?}

\label{lesson:ZH-R18-looking-three-r1}



\begin{quote}
Say \textbf{look}, \textbf{see}, and \textbf{good-looking} in that order.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Hear the three meanings in mixed order. Say each Mandarin answer, read its unpointed card, then write it. Check the neighbour of \zh{看} before deciding the whole meaning.

\section[shū]{Hear \emph{shū} — book}

\label{lesson:ZH-C18-hear-shu}



\begin{quote}
Say \textbf{look}, \textbf{see}, and \textbf{good-looking} in Mandarin.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\emph{shū} — \textbf{book}
\end{quote}

Hold one level first tone. Do not add \emph{kàn} yet; this step is only the object, \textbf{book}. Its four-stroke written form waits until the next lesson.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://hsk.cn-bj.ufileos.com/3.0/\%E6\%96\%B0\%E7\%89\%88HSK\%E8\%80\%83\%E8\%AF\%95\%E5\%A4\%A7\%E7\%BA\%B21219.pdf}{Official HSK 3.0 syllabus, Level 1 vocabulary}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[shū]{\zh{书} — two folds, upright, dot}

\label{lesson:ZH-W18-shu-observe}



\begin{quote}
Say \textbf{book} as \emph{shū}, then write \zh{看} once from memory.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script — the shape}
Write \textbf{\zh{书}} in four strokes: a short horizontal that folds down, a second horizontal that folds and hooks, the long central upright, then the small dot at the upper right. Four strokes; three lifts.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Trace \textbf{\zh{书}} once. Say \textbf{fold, hooked fold, upright, dot}. Let the upright pass through the middle instead of leaning toward the dot.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chanind/hanzi-writer-data/68d10a4b21150cae5e1ebbd223eed289cf32d90c/data/\%E4\%B9\%A6.json}{Hanzi Writer Data \zh{书}, pinned stroke paths and medians}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[shū]{\zh{书} — copy the compact route}

\label{lesson:ZH-W18-shu-guided}



\begin{quote}
Read \textbf{\zh{看见}} and give its meaning. Then air-write \textbf{fold, hooked fold, upright, dot}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Copy \textbf{\zh{书}} twice beside the model. On the second copy, pause before the upright and check that both folds leave a clear central route.

\subsection*{Your turn — Spaced Return}
Hear \textbf{see} and write \zh{看见} once without a model.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chanind/hanzi-writer-data/68d10a4b21150cae5e1ebbd223eed289cf32d90c/data/\%E4\%B9\%A6.json}{Hanzi Writer Data \zh{书}, pinned stroke paths and medians}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[shū]{\zh{书} — wait, then place the dot}

\label{lesson:ZH-W18-shu-delayed}



\begin{quote}
Write \textbf{\zh{好看}} from the meaning \textbf{good-looking}. Then look at \zh{书} for five seconds and cover it.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say \textbf{fold, hooked fold, upright, dot}, then write \textbf{\zh{书}} once without the model. Check only after the dot is in place.

\subsection*{Your turn — Spaced Return}
Hear \textbf{good-looking} and write \zh{好看} without a model.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chanind/hanzi-writer-data/68d10a4b21150cae5e1ebbd223eed289cf32d90c/data/\%E4\%B9\%A6.json}{Hanzi Writer Data \zh{书}, pinned stroke paths and medians}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[shū]{\zh{书} — the sound meets the shape}

\label{lesson:ZH-C18-shu}



\begin{quote}
Say \textbf{book} in Mandarin.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\zh{书}} — \emph{shū} — \textbf{book}
\end{quote}

Hide the pinyin. Read \zh{书}, hold the level first tone, then give its meaning.
\end{cousinweb}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Hear \emph{shū}. Wait three seconds, then write \textbf{\zh{书}} once without a model.

\section[kànshū]{Hear \emph{kànshū} — read a book}

\label{lesson:ZH-C18-hear-kanshu}



\begin{quote}
Say \textbf{look or watch}, then say \textbf{book}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\emph{kànshū} — \textbf{read a book; read books}
\end{quote}

Let \emph{kàn} fall and keep \emph{shū} level. Mandarin says \textbf{look-at + book} for the activity \textbf{read}. Keep the characters hidden for one more tiny step.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://hsk.cn-bj.ufileos.com/3.0/\%E6\%96\%B0\%E7\%89\%88HSK\%E8\%80\%83\%E8\%AF\%95\%E5\%A4\%A7\%E7\%BA\%B21219.pdf}{Official HSK 3.0 syllabus, Level 1 vocabulary}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[kànshū]{\zh{看书} — look at a book, read}

\label{lesson:ZH-C18-kanshu}



\begin{quote}
Say \textbf{read a book} as \emph{kànshū}. Write \zh{看} and \zh{书} separately.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\zh{看书}} — \emph{kànshū} — \textbf{read a book; read books}
\end{quote}

Read the action first and its object second. No new character is hiding here: \zh{看} + \zh{书} gives the whole reading activity.
\end{cousinweb}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Copy \textbf{\zh{看书}} once. Keep the long upright in \zh{书} centred after the denser \zh{看}.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://hsk.cn-bj.ufileos.com/3.0/\%E6\%96\%B0\%E7\%89\%88HSK\%E8\%80\%83\%E8\%AF\%95\%E5\%A4\%A7\%E7\%BA\%B21219.pdf}{Official HSK 3.0 syllabus, Level 1 vocabulary}.
\end{tcolorbox}

\section[Practice]{Payoff — looking and reading}

\label{lesson:ZH-C18-practice}



\begin{quote}
Write \zh{看} and \zh{书} without a model, then name each aloud.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
1. \textbf{Listening, /5:} hear all five forms in mixed order and choose each meaning. 2. \textbf{Speaking, /5:} produce all five from meaning cards, with tones audible. 3. \textbf{Reading, /5:} read \textbf{\zh{看书}, \zh{好看}, \zh{书}, \zh{看见}, \zh{看}} cold, without pinyin. 4. \textbf{Writing, /5:} hear all five meanings and write each form without a model.

Pass each skill separately. Repair only a missed form in the missed skill, then retry that column without cancelling the other three scores.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://hsk.cn-bj.ufileos.com/3.0/\%E6\%96\%B0\%E7\%89\%88HSK\%E8\%80\%83\%E8\%AF\%95\%E5\%A4\%A7\%E7\%BA\%B21219.pdf}{Official HSK 3.0 syllabus, Level 1 vocabulary}.
\end{tcolorbox}
